# F attribute: the recipe is written to a temporary file whose path is passed
# as the last argument to the shell (or the S program), instead of being fed
# on standard input. The file is removed afterwards.
mkdir tmp
env TMPDIR=$WORK/tmp
env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=

# the shell runs the file: $0 is its path
mk -p 1 path
stdout '^script=.*/tmp/mk-path-'
exec ls tmp
! stdout .

# standard input is left to the recipe, so it can read input
exec sh -c '$MK -p 1 reads < input.txt'
stdout '^got hello$'

# with S, the path follows the program's own arguments
mk -p 1 awk
stdout '^awk ran$'

# the default shell still runs with -e; E still removes it
! mk -p 1 stops
! stdout '^after$'
mk -p 1 continues
stdout '^after$'

# -n prints the recipe but creates no file
mk -n -p 1 path
stdout '^path: echo script='
exec ls tmp
! stdout .

-- input.txt --
hello
-- mkfile --
path:VF:
	echo script=$$0

reads:VF:
	read line
	echo got $$line

awk:VFSawk -f:
	BEGIN { print "awk ran" }

stops:VF:
	false
	echo after

continues:VEF:
	false
	echo after
